comment: Golden inputs whose fixtures hold SwaTex's KaTeX-correct values instead of the RaTeX reference's. Every other fixture must match RaTeX exactly. Regenerating a corpus from RaTeX overwrites these rows, so the golden suites will fail until the values here are restored -- this file says which rows and why. Each reason is also listed under "Known limitations" in the README and pinned by a regression test. A row that diverges for more than one reason is listed under one of them, because scripts/diff_layout.py maps each input to a single reason; three align-family rows carrying a \tag are such rows. A divergence is relative to the pinned fixture revision (see "Provenance" in BENCHMARKS.md): where RaTeX has since adopted the same behaviour upstream, the row still diverges from the fixtures and stays listed here. scripts/diff_layout.py reads this file to tell an expected divergence from a regression, and RaTeXDivergenceTests keeps it in step with the corpora.

inputs: \begin{alignat}{2} a &= b & c &= d \\ e &= f & g &= h \end{alignat}
\begin{alignat}{2} x &= y & a &= b \\ &= z & &= c \end{alignat}
\begin{alignedat}{3} a &= b & c &= d & e &= f \end{alignedat}
\begin{aligned} a &= b & c &= d & e &= f \end{aligned}

divergences.reason: an unterminated \verb is a parse error
\limits after an ordinary atom is a parse error
\vcenter centers ink on the math axis, changing display-list depth
a \tag renders in text mode, as KaTeX expands it
a subscript takes the base's italic correction only from a symbol base
